errors.text: Misidentifies the targeted property as high-temperature strength; the target is magnetic coercivity in fcc Fe-Co-Ni-derived high-entropy alloys.

Misstates the orbital-moment challenge as predicting order-disorder kinetics and precipitate stability rather than understanding the orbital moment's contribution to coercivity and magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Replaces the relevant dual-phase fcc/C14 FeCoNiTi system with an unsupported precipitation-hardened fcc matrix containing L12 or B2 precipitates.
Introduces HPHT processing, pressures up to 6 GPa, and 1473 K treatment without relevance to the target study.
Fails to reconstruct the key result of approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K, exceeding the roughly 100 Oe limit of single-phase fcc alloys.
Cited evidence concerns mechanical strengthening in unrelated alloy systems and provides no support for the proposed orbital-moment mechanism.
